quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let other cars pass, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other cars pass, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and enter at the same speed as the traffic moving on the freeway. Always let other traffic pass when you are merging.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: An intersection.
A road curve.
A right turn.
A lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much alcohol you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your body weight. BAC is NOT affected by your physical fitness level or how much alcohol you think you can handle.

questions.question: What should drivers do in a roundabout?

options.text: Let traffic already in the roundabout go first.
Let cars entering the roundabout go first.
Drive clockwise around the circle.
Stop in the middle of the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic already in the roundabout go first.
questions.explanation: In a roundabout, you must let cars already inside the circle pass first. Enter from the right and follow the circle counterclockwise until you reach your exit.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your car is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: How do you avoid hitting cars in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before you turn or change lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to at a crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when told by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.question: You see a problem with your vehicle that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any problem that could affect safe driving right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the problem is fixed.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass cars moving in the same direction.
During the day only.
Anytime.
When you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are turning.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You can only cross solid yellow lines when you are making a turn.

questions.question: What do you do when an emergency vehicle has flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it gets to you.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: Let all emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights pass. Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: This sign prevents:

options.text: Entrance to full parking lots.
Entrance to road construction areas.
Entrance to dead-end streets.
Wrong-direction entries on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong-direction entries on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is one-way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: When passing a parked vehicle, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Honk to alert drivers and pedestrians.
Speed up to avoid pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. Someone may step out or a car may pull out suddenly.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and carefully. Look both ways for traffic before crossing.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then go when the way is clear.

questions.question: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:

options.text: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
It is an ambulance.
It is a school bus.
The vehicle is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back means the vehicle travels slower than 25 mph. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn carriages.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Hide that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how they work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how they work.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, find the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. You may see several of these signs throughout a curve.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Give the vehicle extra space.
Know that the driver is not paying full attention.
Not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If a driver near you seems distracted, stay farther away because they are more likely to have an accident.

questions.question: When visibility is poor, your first action should be:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down first when visibility is poor or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. You should:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass before the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Always let them cross. Be extra careful around children.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: You had an upsetting incident at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. Slow down in school zones, work zones, or bad weather, even if there are no signs.

questions.question: When parallel parking, park your car within ____ inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: Your car's wheels should be within 12 inches of the curb when parallel parking. Park only where it won't block traffic and where other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and go only when it is safe. A stop sign may also be posted at this location.

questions.question: Small children riding in a vehicle:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back.
Won't be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats designed for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use proper car seats for children.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop before entering.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic in the intersection go first before you enter.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look for other vehicles, then go if it is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When passing on a highway with multiple lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift into park.
Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly. When it is safe, pull over and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Leave extra time for your trip.
Follow posted speed limits.
Use turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane on an expressway. When should you move to the left lane?

options.text: When traffic is heavy but moving steadily.
When the weather is bad and roads are slippery.
When traffic is slow in your lane and cars are in the left lane.
When traffic is light and cars are entering from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is light and cars are entering from the right.
questions.explanation: Watch for cars entering the expressway. Move into another lane or slow down to help them merge safely.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashing while driving under the influence of alcohol?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no if someone offers you a drink because you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The only way to avoid driving under the influence is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Once you start drinking, your judgment gets worse, making it hard to make safe choices.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What traffic signal comes after a steady yellow light?

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways on all tracks before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until the train passes.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
School zone.
No passing zone.
Hospital.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers about railroad crossings. Yield to trains and do not try to outrun them.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signals, yield to the vehicle coming from the right.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you need to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt?

options.text: The driver.
A front seat passenger.
Any child under age 16.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The driver, front seat passengers, and all children under 16 must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Keep them straight and set the parking brake.
Turn them away from the curb.
Turn them toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
The beginning of a reduced speed zone.
More pedestrians may be present.
The end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The end of a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign marks the end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, immediately pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Turn the steering wheel carefully to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Turn the steering wheel carefully to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep driving with wheels off the road and gently apply the brakes to reduce speed. When safe, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply turn the wheel or force your vehicle back onto the road.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When conditions are less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the posted speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when any condition makes driving unsafe. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are within the posted limit if you are going too fast for conditions.
